learning: Hypothesis A: lower mass lifts oval progress above 0.1175 without pushing s-bend steering_oscillation above 0.15. Hypothesis B: lower mass over-responds on the s-bend and slalom, so mass 0.8 must be restored. Per-track results will show which holds.
notes: Restores the iteration 3 geometry (y = 0.07, wheel_track 0.12, 16 mm sensors) and changes only mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, as the Builder requested. Controller is unchanged from iteration 3, with no gain change.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.12, y = 0.06) scored 36.76, its worst result since iteration 1. Its s-bend progress fell from 0.165 at y = 0.07 to 0.04, the same as the y = 0.04 baseline, so the forward lead carries the s-bend gain. Under the Integrator rule set in iteration 5, this restores y = 0.07 at wheel_track 0.12, which is the iteration 3 design (score 54.90, s-bend progress 0.165, s-bend steering_oscillation 0.144, under the 0.15 limit). Oval progress has been flat at 0.1175 across every track width and lead change, so mass is the next oval lever. The Builder's requested change is mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg, which lowers yaw inertia (mass times (body_length^2 + body_width^2)/12) and should give a quicker turn response. The controller is unchanged from iterations 3 to 5: kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, sensor_weights 25 times x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), and last_direction line-loss recovery. Only mass changes against iteration 3, so the race isolates that lever. Expected result: oval progress above 0.1175 with max_error near or below 0.06, s-bend progress near 0.165, and s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.15. If s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15, the Builder's rule applies: restore mass 0.8 and test wheel_track 0.11 at y = 0.07.
